source.title: Interpreting and Steering a Text-to-Speech Language Model with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: N. Koriagin; Georgii Aparin; Nikita Balagansky; Daniil Gavrilov

record.tranche_reason: Tests SAE feature recovery and control in a text-to-speech LM, a new setting relative to the toy-model superposition claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports layer-wise SAE modality and reconstruction analyses, held-out auto-interpretation scores, concept probes, and feature-steering outcomes. Probe datasets and candidate-selection results in Appendix G are not recorded as feature-geometry results; results cited from other work are also excluded.
record.test_reason: It trains SAEs on a new kind of LM, a TTS backbone (CosyVoice3/Qwen2.5-0.5B). It reports whether the dictionary recovers interpretable, causally usable sparse features, which bears on V4 in a new setting. No toy-model, capacity or dimensionality tests.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: SAEs on CosyVoice3's LM backbone recover interpretable text-modal, audio-modal and mixed features, and steering some features causally controls laughter, gender and speech rate.
record.recipe_differences: Uses BatchTopK SAEs, modality-aware interpretation, concept probes, and latent-space steering on a TTS LM; it does not reproduce the toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature modality and auto-interpretation scores vary across layers; concept top-1 probe scores also vary by layer and concept.

fits_no_version.finding: The modality makeup of SAE features shifts with depth: mixed features peak at layer 12 (47.3%), layers 16–20 are audio-dominated (74–76%), and layer 23 is 83.1% text-modal.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In multimodal LMs, the modality of SAE features changes systematically across layers.

record.problems: Only one model is studied. The authors note that the labeler and scorer share the same Gemini model, the auto-interpretation sweep is incomplete, speech-token timestamps do not localize sub-token acoustic onsets, and negative sampling may not address representation-neighbor confounds. Numeric uncertainty values are not supplied for the reported steering error bars.

untested.parts: No toy networks, overlap/orthogonality geometry, or sparsity transition.
No test of non-capacity causes of polysemanticity.
No measure of features spread across neurons, and no neuron-vs-SAE comparison. One model only.
No completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, or canonicity tests.
No test of feature dimensionality. Top-1 probes only check whether a single coordinate suffices for a concept.

missing.what: SAE explained variance by layer and token type: overall 0.97–0.99 at layers 0–8, falling to 0.82 at layer 20 and rebounding to 0.945 at layer 23. Text–audio gap is 0.080 at layer 20.
Full SAE-latent probe ROC-AUC for laughter: 0.866 at layer 0, 0.948 at layer 4, ~1.0 from layer 8. Raw-residual probes reach 0.885–1.000.
Top-k (k=5–100) SAE probe results are described in the setup but no values are reported.

record.verdict_notes: V4 is supported only in its 'SAE can recover sparse features' reading. The paper never tests superposition or polysemanticity of neurons directly. Auto-interp uses the same Gemini model as labeler and scorer. Mixed features 'often look polysemantic' (App F). Probe datasets differ between positives and negatives.

versions.untested_parts: No toy-network experiment or test of feature overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry.
No test of capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or polysemanticity arising from capacity pressure.
No test of alternative causes of polysemanticity or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Tests SAE features in one TTS LM backbone only; does not measure feature spread across neurons in general LLMs or establish transfer to other models.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable across settings, or canonical units of the model.
Single-coordinate probes test whether one SAE coordinate can carry concept-prediction signal, but the study does not test the dimensionality or geometry of superposed features.

relationships.condition: Text-modal feature labels across layers; selected layer-20 steering features; top-1 SAE probes at layers 8–16
relationships.reason: Text-modal labels score AUROC 0.90–0.94 (r1, r4). Steering moves laughter, gender and speech rate strongly (r34–r36). Single SAE coordinates reach ~0.91–0.93 ROC-AUC mid-network (r19, r21–r26).
relationships.display_finding: Text-modal labels scored AUROC 0.90–0.94, steering strongly moved laughter, gender and speech rate, and single SAE coordinates reached about 0.91–0.93 ROC-AUC mid-network.

source_check.condition: Text-modal feature labels across layers; selected layer-20 steering features; top-1 SAE probes at layers 8–16
source_check.reason: Text-label AUROC is 0.90–0.94; the specified mid-layer single-coordinate probes reach 0.909–0.929; selected layer-20 features control laughter, gender cues and speech rate.

relationships.condition: Audio-modal and mixed feature labels; top-1 probes at layers 0, 4, 20, 23 and some mid-layer concepts
relationships.reason: Audio labels only reach 0.65–0.72 and mixed labels 0.53–0.69 (r2, r3, r5, r6). No single SAE coordinate separates the concepts at layer 0 (r13–r15, ~0.51), and top-1 scores are lower at other layers (r16–r18, r20, r27–r33). The judge is circular (same Gemini model labels and scores).
relationships.display_finding: Audio labels scored only 0.65–0.72 and mixed labels 0.53–0.69. At layer 0, no single SAE coordinate separated the concepts (about 0.51), and top-1 scores were lower at other layers. The same Gemini model both labelled and scored the features, so the judge is circular.

tranche.reason: Tests SAE recovery of interpretable sparse features in a new setting: the residual stream of a generative TTS language-model backbone.

source_check.notes: Probe baselines are not explicitly reported as chance; the pack's suggested baseline fixes are inferred. Positive and negative probe examples come from different datasets. The paper also inconsistently describes backbone depth and whether speech-prompt states are modified during steering prefill.
